prompt: A figure has a $7 \times 4$ rectangle stacked on top of a $10 \times 3$ rectangle. **Total area**?
hint: Stacking one rectangle on another makes a composite figure. Its area is the areas of the parts put together.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try easier numbers first: a $2 \times 1$ rectangle stacked on a $3 \times 1$ rectangle covers $2 + 3 = 5$ squares in all.
Stacking one rectangle on another makes a composite figure. Its area is the areas of the parts put together.
The top rectangle has area $7 \times 4 = 28$ and the bottom rectangle has area $10 \times 3 = 30$. Add these two numbers.
$28 + 30 = 58$, so the total area of the figure is $58$ square units.

explanation: Find the area of the top rectangle: $7 \times 4 = 28$.
Find the area of the bottom rectangle: $10 \times 3 = 30$.
The rectangles touch but do not overlap, so add their areas: $28 + 30 = 58$.
The total area of the figure is $58$ square units.
